transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I came in because my mind keeps going blank, and it happens at the worst times. I work as a flagger, and lately, I'll look at the road-closure forms or even just my stop-slow paddle, and... I suddenly cannot remember the steps. It's just things I have done for years, but the thoughts are just gone.
Did something very upsetting or frightening happen shortly before these blank spells started?

No... I can't think of anything like that. I mean, nothing frightening or really upsetting happened right before they started. I've just been doing my normal routine, going to work and coming home. They just sort of... started happening on their own.
When your mind goes blank, do you feel very anxious right then?

No, I wouldn't say I feel anxious when it happens. It's more like... my brain just switches off. I don't feel panicked or anything right in that moment. There's just simply nothing there, like a complete blank.
Outside of those blank moments, have you been getting confused about everyday things?

No, not really. I mean, I know how to make my coffee, I know how to drive to work, I pay my bills... it's just those specific moments where everything drops out. The rest of the time, I'm just doing my normal stuff without any trouble.
Have you had any head injury around the time these blank spells began?
No, I haven't. I haven't hit my head or been in any kind of accident or anything like that.
During these blank spells, do you stay aware of what is happening around you?
No, not really. It's like I'm just... paused. I don't really know what's going on around me until I sort of snap back to it.
After one of these blank spells, do you ever realize that you cannot account for a period of time that has passed?

No, I don't think so. I mean, it's not like hours have gone by or anything. It just feels like a quick pause... maybe a few seconds. I don't ever look at the clock and feel like I've lost a whole chunk of time.
During one of these blank spells, have other people ever told you that you were making repetitive movements, like lip-smacking, chewing, or fumbling with your hands?
No, no one has ever mentioned anything like that to me. I don't think I do any of those things, just... stare off, I guess. No one's said anything about chewing or moving my hands.
Do you completely lose consciousness during these blank spells?
No, I don't pass out or anything like that. I'm still awake, just... zoned out, I guess. I don't lose consciousness.
Do these blank spells happen only when you are dealing with work-related things like your road-closure forms or stop-slow paddle?

No, it's not just when I'm at work. But... that is why I came in. My mind just keeps going blank at the worst times. Like, I'll look at the road-closure forms or the stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I just cannot remember the steps. And I've done this job for years. It's just... gone.
Has anyone ever told you that during these blank spells you just stare and do not respond when they talk to you?

No, nobody's ever said that to me. I mean, I live alone, so there isn't really anyone around to notice if I'm just staring and not responding. And at work, I'm usually out on the road by myself, so... no, I haven't heard that from anyone.
After one of these blank spells, do you feel confused?

No, I wouldn't say I feel confused afterward. It's more just... frustrating. I just kind of snap back to it and realize I lost my train of thought. But I know where I am and what I'm supposed to be doing, I just have to figure out where I left off. So, no, not confused.
Have you had times when you could not remember important things about your own life, like personal events or parts of your past?

No, I haven't had anything like that. I remember my past and personal events just fine. It's really just... what I'm doing in the moment that slips away, like I was saying before. But I haven't forgotten any important parts of my life or anything like that.
Have you been having trouble remembering things that happened just a short time ago?

No, not really. I mean, if you mean something that happened yesterday or a few hours ago, I can remember that fine. It's just... like I said, losing my train of thought right in the middle of doing something. But I'm not forgetting conversations I just had or what I ate for breakfast. My short-term memory seems okay, as far as I can tell.
Have you ever been told that you have seizures or epilepsy?
No, I've never been told anything like that. No seizures or epilepsy. I've never had any medical issues like that brought up by a doctor before.
When one of these blank spells happens, do you have trouble finding the right words or naming familiar objects?

No, I don't think so. I mean, when my mind goes blank, I'm just... stuck. It's not that I can't remember what a cup is called, it's just that the whole thought is gone. So, no, I don't really have trouble finding words for things.
Have you had any tests like an EEG or brain scan that showed a problem with your brain?
No, I haven't. I've never had an EEG or an MRI or anything like that done on my brain. No doctor has ever ordered one or said I needed one.
Right before one of these blank spells, do you ever notice a strange smell or taste?
No, I haven't noticed anything like that. No weird smells or tastes or anything right before it happens. Just the thought disappearing.
Do these blank spells tend to happen in the exact same way each time?

I'm not really sure if it's exactly the same every time. I mean, the result is always the same—I just stop, and the thought is completely gone. But I haven't really noticed if there's a specific pattern to it or if it happens in the exact same way. It just kind of... happens.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical condition that affects the brain or nerves?
No, I haven't. I've never been diagnosed with any kind of medical condition like that... nothing to do with my brain or my nerves.

Dissociative disorder is less supported because no traumatic or psychosocial precipitant was identified and there is no loss of personal memory. Other specified mental disorders due to brain damage/dysfunction are less supported because no neurological condition, head injury, or abnormal testing was reported.
